points.title: Technical specification
points.must: A document written at the design stage listing the hardware and software needed to run the new system, with figures (GB, GHz) and a reason for every choice.

points.title: Minimum and recommended requirements
points.must: Minimum: the lowest hardware on which the software still runs; recommended: higher, runs comfortably; the specification is never below the minimum.

points.title: Hardware components
points.must: Processor (cores, GHz), RAM (GB), storage (SSD/HDD, GB), display (resolution), network (card, Mbps), input and output devices, UPS / backup.

points.title: Rule for the processor
points.must: Take the highest processor requirement of all the software; speeds are never added.

points.title: Rule for RAM
points.must: Add the RAM of the OS and all programs that run at the same time; round up to a standard size (e.g. 7 GB → 8 GB).

points.title: Rule for storage
points.must: Add all software + the data now + the growth of the data over the life of the system (+ backups).

points.title: Worked calculation
points.must: A full example with figures, e.g. 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 → 8 GB RAM; 69 GB software + 16 GB data → 128 GB.

points.title: Peripherals from inputs and outputs
points.must: Input and output devices chosen from the system's inputs/outputs, each with a reason (barcode scanner, receipt printer, card reader).

points.title: SSD and HDD
points.must: SSD: faster access, no moving parts, good for databases; HDD: cheaper per GB, good for backups.

points.title: System and application software
points.must: System software runs the computer (OS, utilities: antivirus, backup); application software does the user's task (DBMS, booking program).

points.title: Off-the-shelf and bespoke
points.must: Off-the-shelf: cheaper, available now, tested, may not fit exactly; bespoke: fits exactly, expensive, slow to develop.

points.title: Open source and proprietary
points.must: Open source: code available, usually free, community support; proprietary: closed code, licence fee, official support; freeware is free but closed.

points.title: Criteria for choosing software
points.must: Functionality, compatibility, cost, ease of use, support, security, scalability, multi-user access.

points.title: Writing a justification
points.must: Software → criterion → 'because' + a need of the scenario, with one worked example.

points.title: Why specify above the minimum
points.must: Growth of data, more users, software updates, several programs at once, performance — but not the most expensive without reason.
